title: Pull a flush shower drain grate with its lifting hook, lay it on the mat, and put the hook back
instruction: Use the lifting hook to pull the flush stainless shower drain grate out, lay it flat on the mat, and put the hook back in its holder.
context: Bathroom cleaners and householders lift a flush shower-drain grate with the small hook sold with it to clear hair from the strainer underneath; plumbing guides describe this as the standard way to open such a cover (https://www.mrrooter.com/about/blog/how-to-remove-a-shower-drain-cover/). No job headcount is claimed. Related pending tasks differ in the ability tested: our pop-up stopper hair wand task (clear hair from under a sink stopper) draws hair out under a stopper head, and the flush plate nest task (push a flush plate out of its nest, then take it by the overhang) shoves a plate out of a nest; here a hook is fed blind through a slot, turned a quarter turn under a rib and used to lift a 0.24 kg flush plate level.
setup: Positions are object centres in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left (negative toward the right arm). Table: wood top, about 110 x 130 cm, arm bases 61 cm apart on its near edge. Floor drain deck: 17.6 x 21.6 cm, 4 cm tall blue-white ceramic tile slab with dark grout lines (x 16.2 to 33.8, y -23.8 to -2.2), holding a 304 stainless square drain (Elegante KD01A113-6, https://www.homedepot.com/p/321473973) centred at x 25, y -10.6: 15.2 cm frame, 14.2 cm recess 1.5 cm deep, 1 cm ledge, 12.2 cm dark well. Grate: 304 stainless, 13.6 x 13.6 x 1.5 cm, 0.24 kg, 7 mm skirt, five bars along x (12, 10, 10, 9, 9 mm), two 6 mm cross bars, 18 slots; it lies in the recess, 3 mm play per side, flush with the tile, centred at x 25, y -10.6; the slot beside the middle bar on the robot's side is 36 x 13 mm. Lifting hook: stainless, 88 mm long, 22 x 7 x 4 mm foot, 6 mm round shaft, 22 x 30 x 14 mm T-handle with an orange silicone sleeve, 55 g; it stands foot down in a charcoal silicone holder (6.0 x 4.4 x 3.4 cm, 30 x 13 mm slot 3 cm deep) at x 25, y -21 on the right tile strip, leaning 8 degrees against the slot's near end. Service mat: charcoal silicone, 17.6 x 15.4 x 1 cm, centred at x 25, y 6.5.
scoring: Score 0 if the grate is ever more than 35 degrees from upright for 0.15 s, the grate or the hook leaves x 10 to 42 cm or |y| 28 cm, the grate lies on the bare table, or the grate is lifted 1 cm clear of the tile with the hook not under it. Otherwise, at the end, with the fingers 3 cm or more clear and everything still for 2 s: 1.0 the grate flat on the mat (within 5 degrees, 25 mm of its centre, wholly on the mat) and the hook standing in its holder (foot in the slot, shaft within 40 degrees of upright); 0.75 grate on the mat, hook 5 cm or more from it but not in the holder; 0.50 grate on the mat, hook still on or beside it; 0.40 the grate was lifted 1 cm clear of the tile and level (within 25 degrees) on the hook for 0.25 s but is not on the mat; 0 otherwise.
reset_notes: Drop the grate back into the recess, stand the hook in its holder leaning on the near end of the slot, wipe the foot and the grate's underside dry. Dry bench rig: no water or soap.
fidelity: Rigid parts, no water. The holder and mat are bench conveniences; most credit comes from the blind lift (0.40), the put-away adds only 0.25. Ribs (5 mm) and hook foot (4 mm) are thicker than real 1.5 mm sheet, but foot-in-slot (3 mm a side) and rib clearance (1.5 mm) are real-sized. Hook dimensions are estimated; see README.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (reached over the drain with the right arm, grate left in its recess); demo: 1 (lifted the grate with the hook, laid it on the mat, stood the hook in its holder)
